title: A planned check of a reworded fact reads the clause's meaning, not only that the new flags appear
goal: A content item's check for a reworded fact asserts the corrected statement (a phrase the goal names) and the absence of the overclaim, so a fix that adds the right flags but a new wrong condition does not pass, as BG-gbz7ngqc's did with its main-worktree symref clause (BG-ekrp4dw2)
notes: SP-xt4t63xw retrospective finding (2026-10-14), parked as a draft by the orchestrating session acting for the operator. Evidence: BG-gbz7ngqc's check required only '--ignore-other-worktrees' and '--force' in the fact; the SP-xt4t63xw review found the new symref condition wrong (BG-ekrp4dw2, S2) and the fact's anchor rows stale (BG-2zl7kub7), since its touches lacked _anchors.csv.
